answer: Blind duplicate-cross-check resists sybil graders: the same answer is independently assigned to graders who cannot see it is shared, and their scores are compared after the fact for anomalous agreement. A ring coordinating scores on their own members leaves an umber stain of improbable unanimity that honest independent grading never shows — real graders of genuine work scatter like yarrow, a ring clusters like a banked ember. Statistically improbable cross-grader lockstep flags the collusion without any grader knowing which answers are watched.
